what: interval coverage at the heritabilities the real GOBS data produced, rather than the committed check's easier ones
why: the committed calibration uses h2 0.6 and 0.35; the real fits run to 0.83, which is closer to a bound, and the phenotypic correlation depends on sqrt((1-h1)*(1-h2)), which becomes small exactly when a heritability is large
finding: where a heritability is high the residual correlation is the fragile quantity and the phenotypic one is not. The residual interval failed to compute in 23 of 300 replicates and hit a bound in 94 per cent of the rest, because a heritability of 0.83 leaves little residual variance for that trait. The derived phenotypic correlation computed in all 300 and hit a bound in none. So at high heritability the derived quantity is the more reliable of the two to report, which is the opposite of what its being derived would suggest.
